children.name: Article Title
children.text: Cluster nodes, kubeconfig, and join tokens

children.name: Article Lead
children.text: Read node health and capacity, protect administrative access, and add workers only when cluster operations are enabled.

children.name: Article Callout Text
children.text: Kubeconfig and node-join tokens are administrative credentials; keep them out of tickets, chat, logs, and shell history.

children.name: Section Body 1
children.text: Confirm distribution, version, ready count, roles, pressure, uptime, pod capacity, CPU, and memory on the Nodes page (v0.4.0).

children.name: Section 1 Item Text 0
children.text: Treat NotReady and pressure as Kubernetes-level triage.

children.name: Section 1 Item Text 1
children.text: Compare allocatable capacity with GameServer requests.

children.name: Section 1 Item Text 2
children.text: Preserve headroom for control plane, ingress, agents, and backup jobs.

children.name: Section Body 2
children.text: The action requires clusterOps.enabled and an authorized role. Replace a standalone registration by PUT, never by delete and re-register (v0.4.0).

children.name: Section 2 Item Text 0
children.text: Verify context before use and start with read-only commands.

children.name: Section 2 Item Text 1
children.text: Store with restrictive permissions; never attach to support tickets.

children.name: Section 2 Item Text 2
children.text: Record recipients and revoke underlying access when no longer needed.

children.name: Section Body 3
children.text: Mint a short-lived token for the intended cluster, run the generated join procedure, then verify readiness and one test workload.

children.name: Quick Reference Line 1
children.text: 01  Read version, Ready, roles, pressure, pods, CPU, memory

children.name: Quick Reference Line 2
children.text: 02  Kubeconfig requires clusterOps.enabled; handle as admin secret

children.name: Quick Reference Line 3
children.text: 03  Join token → Ready + labels/taints/capacity + test workload
